before.title: Front Lower Control Arm / Tension Rod Bushing Wear
before.description: A common wear issue on the Y51 chassis is deterioration of the front lower control arm and tension rod bushings, which leads to looseness under braking and over bumps. The heavy V8 front-end load accelerates bushing cracking and fluid-filled bushing failure, causing alignment instability and uneven tire wear.
before.solution: Diagnosis involves inspecting the front suspension for torn bushings, checking for wheel movement under pry-bar load, and road-testing for brake shimmy or clunks. Repair usually means replacing the affected control arms or tension rods as complete assemblies, followed by a four-wheel alignment; typical cost is about $500 to $1,400 depending on how many arms are replaced and whether OEM or aftermarket parts are used.

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for Infiniti M56 suspension/steering concerns

communityRecommendations.content: Owners often replace the whole arm instead of pressing bushings because it saves labor and restores ball joint condition at the same time.
Moog components are commonly recommended for daily-driven cars when OEM pricing is too high.
Have alignment checked immediately after arm replacement; owners report rapid tire wear if toe is left out of spec.

before.title: Radiator / Cooling Fan Module Failure
before.description: M56 owners report overheating or rising coolant temperature caused by radiator leakage and/or electric cooling fan control failure. The issue is typically related to age-related plastic tank cracking, fan motor wear, or failure of the integrated fan control assembly, especially in hot climates or stop-and-go driving.
before.solution: Diagnosis includes pressure-testing the cooling system, checking for seepage at radiator end tanks, and commanding fan operation with a scan tool. Repairs usually involve replacing the radiator and/or fan assembly, refilling with the correct Nissan/Infiniti blue coolant, and bleeding the system; typical cost ranges from about $700 to $1,800 depending on which components fail.
symptoms: Coolant smell or visible coolant leak

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for Infiniti M56 involving overheating/cooling issues

communityRecommendations.content: Owners often choose a complete replacement fan assembly to avoid repeat labor when only one motor or the controller is weak.
If the temperature climbs mainly at idle but drops at speed, inspect fan operation before assuming a thermostat problem.
For radiator replacement, owners prefer OE-style units with proper hose neck fitment and transmission cooler compatibility.

before.title: Steering Rack / Power Steering Leak and Noise
before.description: Some M56 owners report power steering fluid leaks, groaning, or inconsistent steering assist caused by rack seal leakage or hose seepage. As fluid level drops, the pump can become noisy and steering effort increases, particularly during parking maneuvers.
before.solution: Diagnosis includes inspecting rack boots and hydraulic lines for fluid, checking reservoir level and condition, and listening for pump cavitation. Repair may involve replacing leaking pressure hoses or the steering rack assembly, then flushing and refilling with the correct fluid; costs typically range from about $300 for hose-related repairs to $1,800 for a rack replacement.
symptoms: Wet steering rack boots or lines

citations.title: NHTSA complaints involving steering issues on Infiniti M56

communityRecommendations.content: Do not keep topping off fluid without finding the leak; owners report pumps often become noisy after running low even once.
For hose seepage, owners often start with replacing the pressure line before committing to a full rack replacement.
If the rack boots contain fluid, the internal rack seals are usually failing and hose replacement alone will not solve it.

before.title: Timing Chain Guide Wear / Chain Noise
before.description: Owners of VK56VD-equipped M56 models report startup rattle and persistent front-engine timing noise related to timing chain guide and tensioner wear. As mileage increases, slack in the primary chain system can affect valve timing and trigger correlation faults, especially when oil change intervals have been extended.
before.solution: Diagnosis starts with confirming cold-start rattle, checking oil condition/pressure, and scanning for cam/crank correlation codes. Repair typically involves replacing the timing chains, guides, and tensioners, and resealing the front cover; on this engine the labor is substantial, so total repair commonly runs from about $2,500 to $5,000 depending on parts replaced and shop rate.
symptoms: Rattle from front of engine on cold start

citations.title: NHTSA complaints mentioning timing chain / engine noise on Infiniti M56

communityRecommendations.content: Use high-quality synthetic oil and avoid extended oil intervals; owners report chain noise is more common on engines with inconsistent maintenance.
Owners typically replace the full timing service set rather than only one guide because labor overlap is high and partial repairs often lead to repeat teardown.
If startup rattle lasts more than a brief second, inspect immediately to avoid chain jump and more severe engine damage.

before.title: TPMS Sensor Battery Failure
before.description: As these vehicles age, the original tire pressure monitoring sensors commonly fail when their internal batteries are depleted. This causes the TPMS warning light to flash and then stay on, even when tire pressures are correct, and is a frequent owner-reported nuisance on 2011-2013 cars.
before.solution: Diagnosis is performed with a TPMS scan tool to identify the dead or non-communicating sensor(s). Repair involves replacing the failed sensor(s), installing new seals if reusing serviceable hardware, and registering the IDs to the vehicle; typical cost is about $80 to $300 depending on how many sensors are replaced and whether programming is needed.
symptoms: TPMS light flashing then staying on
No tire pressure data from one or more wheels
Intermittent TPMS faults in cold weather

citations.title: NHTSA complaints mentioning TPMS warning issues on Infiniti M56

communityRecommendations.content: Owners often replace all four sensors during a tire change once the originals begin failing because the batteries tend to expire around the same age.
Have the shop verify sensor IDs and relearn procedure after installation; many repeat warnings are caused by programming issues rather than bad new sensors.
If one original sensor has failed and the others are the same age, budget for the rest soon.
